subject: Animation
title: Steve Jobs and the Business of Dreams
description: A short lesson to help you apply Steve Jobs and the Business of Dreams.

hook.text: Steve Jobs bought Pixar hoping to sell hardware. The company lost money for nearly a decade instead.

buildup.text: Jobs poured over $50 million of his own money into Pixar while it struggled to find a business model.

discovery.text: Toy Story's success in 1995 finally made Pixar profitable and turned Jobs into a billionaire overnight.

twist.text: Jobs originally wanted to shut down the animation side. He changed his mind only after seeing the work.

climax.text: When Disney bought Pixar in 2006 for $7.4 billion, Jobs became Disney's largest shareholder.

punchline.text: A $5 million gamble became a $7.4 billion empire.

quiz.question: What was Steve Jobs's original plan for Pixar?
options: To make animated films from the start
To sell hardware — he nearly shut down the animation division before changing his mind
To compete directly with Disney in theme parks

details.summary: Steve Jobs purchased Pixar from Lucasfilm in 1986 and funded it through years of losses before Toy Story's success. His investment of over $50 million and his negotiation of the Disney distribution deal created the business foundation for Pixar's creative independence.
details.whyItMatters: Without Jobs' financial patience and business acumen, Pixar would have folded before making a single film. His willingness to fund creative vision without immediate returns is a model for how business can support art.
takeaways: Jobs bought Pixar for $5 million and invested over $50 million before profitability
He negotiated the crucial Disney distribution deal that made Toy Story possible
His financial patience funded years of creative development without returns

faq.question: Why did Steve Jobs keep funding Pixar despite years of losses?
faq.answer: Jobs believed in the vision of computer-animated filmmaking even as Pixar bled money selling hardware and software. He repeatedly funded the company from personal wealth, convinced that the technology would eventually produce entertainment that justified the investment.

faq.question: How did Jobs' business skills help Pixar creatively?
faq.answer: Jobs negotiated increasingly favorable deals with Disney that gave Pixar creative control and profit sharing. This independence let Pixar make films their way without studio interference — a creative freedom that most animation studios never enjoy.
